title: Share DART projectile flight across game, Sentry range and Units
context: Quiver and Heptapod still used procedural cones in the real game and curved points in Units while the Sentry range used the pinned DART model. The owner requested unified projectiles.
outcome: Added one launch/timing/presentation owner, used by all three consumers. A pure sphere log/exp adapter preserves ground arcs, radial heights, measured muzzle launch direction and moving endpoints in gameplay. Game missile damage lands on configured arrival for a surviving target; dead targets retain their last endpoint without retargeted damage. Quiver uses the shared upward launch elevation; Heptapod launches from real vertical cassette sockets. Instances return to bounded pools on arrival, restart, unit changes or disposal. Units and game read immutable shipped settings; no user working copy was promoted. Acquisition/lock rules remain existing game rules; lab engagement bounds still require a separate board-unit contract.
alternatives: Replacing only the cone/dot meshes would preserve the three divergent flight implementations and leave timing/ignition inconsistent.
Tank shells and other Units schematic weapon previews remain outside this missile correction.
evidence: npm run check and npm run build.
npm run test:browser: gameplay DART with A6 Terraformer and MORK, Quiver/Heptapod Units previews, pool cleanup and existing Sentry flight checks.
test/sphere-missile-flight.mjs: poles, antipodal endpoints, moving targets, finite unit directions, exact endpoints and flat parity.

Initial browser runs failed the MORK recoil assertion: the expanded acceptance hook returned fireShell instead of invoking it. Corrected the hook; the ordinary fire button was unaffected. Replaced the fixed 120 ms assertion with a bounded wait for recoil.
